brown.title: The IDC Seismic, Hydroacoustic and Infrasound Global Low and High Noise Models
brown.provenance: Approximate digitization of the solid IDC hydroacoustic curves, not official numerical model data.
brown.figure_license: CC BY 2.0; Brown, Ceranna, Prior, Mialle and Le Bras
brown.comparison_band: Bins centred at or above 0.2 Hz (below 0.2 Hz Webb 1998 Fig. 2 is used) with full smoothing-bin support inside the digitized curve; no extrapolation.
brown.applicability: In-water IMS hydrophone statistical curves, not universal seafloor pressure acceptance limits. Low/high are station 5th/95th percentile envelopes across the network.

reviewed_20261019.method: Manual samples of the two solid curves using the original 123..831 x and 15..723 y pixel axes. Original 17 samples retained; 20 added. No shipping dashed curves. Pixel precision is not physical accuracy. 2 dB is a review flag, not a certified error bound.

brown.check_20261026: Project instruction values 1 Hz -25..-2, 10 Hz -49..-25, 100 Hz -56..-38 dB match this digitization within its 2 dB tolerance.

webb.title: Broadband seismology and noise under the ocean
webb.citation: Webb, S. C. (1998), Rev. Geophys., 36(1), 105-142, Figure 2 (non-Arctic: Pacific and Atlantic)
webb.provenance: Low/high bounds read from Webb (1998) Figure 2 Pacific and Atlantic curves, as given in the project instructions (screenshot 2026-10-26) and checked against the figure: 0.005 Hz Atlantic ~3e3, Pacific ~6e4 Pa^2/Hz; 0.05 Hz ~0.3-0.5 Pa^2/Hz; 0.1 Hz ~1-100 Pa^2/Hz; 0.2 Hz Atlantic ~7e2, Pacific ~4e4 Pa^2/Hz.
webb.supplied_by: Project instructions (Wayne Crawford), source Webb (1998) Fig. 2
webb.comparison_band: Discrete figure-read points at or below 0.2 Hz; no interpolation in the comparison. Brown et al. is used above 0.2 Hz.

superseded_20261026.title: Unverified project handout values attributed to Webb
superseded_20261026.provenance: Bounds transcribed from the user-supplied instructions attributed to Webb. Review of the author-uploaded 1991 paper did not establish this table as a published universal low/high model.
